meta.title: About Alan Belferrag — HPC & Cloud Infrastructure
meta.description: Alan Belferrag is an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer working independently on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC consulting.

hero.description: I’m Alan Belferrag, an HPC and cloud infrastructure engineer. In my day job, I’m a Research Computing Specialist in university research computing; this site is for my separate, independent consulting work. My project work includes RGCP: A Self-Service GPU Compute Bridge and the design of ACC: A Production Azure HPC Platform. I work directly with clients on GPU infrastructure and cloud HPC.

whatYouGet.heading: Two infrastructure projects
whatYouGet.lead: These case studies describe the GPU compute and cloud HPC work behind my consulting focus.

items.title: RGCP: GPU compute
items.description: A self-service GPU cloud platform with cost governance, usage visibility, limits, and onboarding for researchers during an on-prem hardware transition.

items.title: ACC: Azure HPC design
items.description: Design of an Azure CycleCloud and Slurm platform for research workloads, including scheduling, storage, identity, budget controls, and scientific software.

items.title: Scheduling and workload fit
items.description: The ACC design used one homogeneous compute pool and Slurm policies to accommodate both multi-node MPI and memory-heavy single-node jobs.

items.title: Cost controls
items.description: Both projects treated spend as an infrastructure concern, using limits, visibility, capacity planning, or scale-to-zero design where appropriate.

items.title: Researcher access and onboarding
items.description: The platforms were designed around researchers who needed usable compute environments, with institutional access and onboarding considered as part of the work.

items.title: Shared software environments
items.description: The ACC design used centrally managed Spack and Lmod modules and reusable environments across autoscaled compute nodes.

items.title: Validation and monitoring
items.description: The ACC platform was deployed and validated with production monitoring and representative multi-node MPI benchmarking.

items.title: Cloud storage design
items.description: The ACC design included persistent home storage and high-performance parallel scratch for research workloads.

items.title: Independent consulting
items.description: This is my personal consulting work, separate from my university role. I work directly with clients.

principles.heading: Design around the workload
principles.lead: The project work reflects practical choices about operations, workload mix, and cost constraints.

items.title: Fit the operating model
items.description: Choose orchestration and automation with the size and capacity of the team operating the platform in mind.

items.title: Fit the workload mix
items.description: Account for both tightly coupled MPI jobs and memory-heavy single-node workloads when shaping the cluster and scheduler policy.

items.title: Plan for cost limits
items.description: Use capacity planning and visible usage controls rather than treating cloud compute as an unconstrained resource.

stack.title: HPC and cloud infrastructure
stack.description: Project experience described here includes Azure CycleCloud, Slurm, MPI, Spack, Lmod, and HyperStack, alongside cloud cluster design for research workloads.

faq.lead: A few practical details about the work and how I operate.

items.answer: I review GPU and model-serving spend, identify opportunities to reduce GPU or token costs, and help implement changes. The scope and savings baseline need to be agreed for each engagement.

items.question: Is there an upfront fee for that offer?
items.answer: No upfront fee for the GPU cost-reduction offer. Payment is due only after I have demonstrated real savings.

items.answer: Cluster and cloud-compute planning and design for research-oriented organizations, including Slurm-based environments on platforms such as AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.

items.answer: The ACC case study describes my Azure HPC platform design work.

meta.title: HPC and GPU Infrastructure Consulting — Alan Belferrag
meta.description: GPU infrastructure and demonstrated-savings cost reduction for AI teams, plus cloud HPC consulting for research and engineering organizations.

hero.description: I help AI teams address GPU and token spend, and help research and engineering organizations plan cloud HPC environments.

design.heading: GPU cost reduction for AI teams
paragraphs: GPU capacity and model-serving costs can be difficult to understand and control as an AI workload grows. I review how compute is being used, identify opportunities to reduce GPU and token spend, and help put changes into practice.

For this specific cost-reduction offer, there is no upfront fee. Payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings. The RGCP case study describes my work building self-service GPU compute with cost governance.

included.text: examine GPU and model-serving usage and establish an agreed baseline.
identify changes that could reduce GPU or token spend while taking workload needs into account.
agree the comparison method, apply the changes, and assess the demonstrated savings.

included.lead: No upfront fee for this offer
included.text: payment is due only after I demonstrate real savings.
see RGCP for an example of GPU compute provisioning and cost governance.

development.heading: Cloud HPC consulting
paragraphs: Research and engineering teams need cloud compute that fits their workloads, operational capacity, security requirements, and budget. I help plan and design cluster and cloud-compute environments, including Slurm-based platforms using services such as AWS ParallelCluster or Azure CycleCloud.
The ACC case study describes my design for an Azure CycleCloud-managed Slurm platform, including scheduling policy, storage, identity, budget controls, and scientific software environments.

included.text: plan the cloud HPC platform and its operational model around the organization’s needs.
consider multi-node MPI and memory-heavy single-node jobs in the Slurm design.
plan shared research storage and centrally managed scientific software where required.
account for institutional access, identity requirements, capacity limits, and cost controls.
see ACC for an example of Azure cloud HPC platform design.

performance.heading: Cost controls for compute platforms
paragraphs: Cloud platforms need practical limits and visibility to prevent unplanned spend. I account for capacity and cost controls as part of infrastructure design, rather than treating them as reporting to add later.
The right measures depend on the workload and operating model. The RGCP and ACC case studies show examples of usage limits, capacity planning, and scale-to-zero design in different compute contexts.

included.text: make compute use visible to the people responsible for cost and capacity.
consider enforceable usage limits or project budgets where appropriate.
match capacity decisions to the workload, project constraints, and expected use.
consider autoscaling or scale-to-zero for temporary and variable workloads.
for the GPU cost-reduction offer, payment is due only after demonstrated savings.

process.lead: We can define the need, constraints, scope, and a way to evaluate the work before deciding whether to proceed.
